headline: Approved Lifebridge Main Campus design and 24 Congress Street facade changes; continued several projects, including 16 Bridge Street.
summary: Approved facade painting and new entry doors at 24 Congress Street, and the Lifebridge Main Campus design, with open design questions sent to the Planning Board. Approved a temporary sign extension request for 231-251 Washington Street. Continued projects at 6 Front Street, 194 Essex Street, 211 Bridge Street, 16 Bridge Street, and the Highland Avenue car wash site.
decisions: Approved a temporary sign permit extension for Levana Group leasing signage at 231-251 Washington Street, 6-0.
Continued the review of replacing 34 windows at 6 Front Street, 6-0.
Continued the facade trim painting review at 194 Essex Street, Unit 171, World of Wizardy, 6-0.
Continued the restoration of seven windows at 211 Bridge Street at the applicant's request, 6-0.
Approved facade painting, tile trim, and new entry doors at 24 Congress Street, 5-0 with one member absent for the vote.
Approved the Lifebridge Main Campus design as presented at 56 Margin Street, with open design questions sent to the Planning Board, 6-0.
Continued the review of a two-family residential building at 16 Bridge Street, 6-0.
Continued the review of the car wash facility on Highland Avenue, with the topics discussed, 6-0.

DRB 
October 28, 2026 
Page 1 of 8 
 
City of Salem Massachusetts 
Public Meeting Minutes 
 
Board or Committee:   Design Review Board, Regular Meeting 
Date and Time:    Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 6:00 pm 
Meeting Location:   Virtual Zoom Meeting 
DRB Members Present: Chair Paul Durand, Catherine Miller, Elizabeth Murray, Marc 
Perras, Sarah Tarbet, and Joseph Badowski 
DRB Members Absent: Daniel Estes 
Others Present: Stephanie Owens, Senior Planner 
Recorder:  Christine Petryszyn 
 
The meeting was called to order at 6:00pm. Roll call was taken  
 
Joseph Badowski joined at 6:01pm. 
 
Signs in the Urban Renewal Area 
1. 231-251 Washington Street: Levana Group Leasing Signage  
 
Justin Steele was present to discuss the proposal:  
• Mr. Steele noted that he was requesting a three-month extension on their temporary sign 
permit.  
• The property is for lease and the request is to put up a 6’ by 2’ banner on two sides of the 
building for marketing purposes.  
• Mr. Steele said there has been quite a bit of interest, but they are still in full marketing mode 
with no tenant lined up.  
• Mr. Steele said that their right to lease agreement is for another three months.  
 
There were no comments or questions from members of the public.  
 
 VOTE: Ms. Miller made a motion to approve.  
 Seconded by Mr. Perras.  
Roll Call: Badowski, Miller, Murray, Perras, Tarbet, and Durand. 6-0 in favor. 
 
  
Projects in the Urban Renewal Area 
 
1. 6 Front Street: Small Project Review – Replacement of 34 windows on the second and third floors of 
the property. 
 
 VOTE: Mr. Perras made a motion to continue.  
 Seconded by Ms. Miller.  
Roll Call: Badowski, Miller, Murray, Perras, Tarbet, and Durand. 6-0 in favor.
DRB 
October 28, 2026 
Page 2 of 8 
 
2. 194 Essex Street, Unit 171, World of Wizardy: Small Project Review – Facade trim painting at World 
of Wizardry.  
 
The applicant was not present.  
 
 VOTE: Mr. Perras made a motion to continue.  
 Seconded by Ms. Miller.  
Roll Call: Badowski, Miller, Murray, Perras, Tarbet, and Durand. 6-0 in favor. 
 
3. 211 Bridge Street: Small Project Review – Restoration of seven windows on the southern facade.  
 
The applicant requested to continue to the November meeting.  
 
 VOTE: Mr. Perras made a motion to continue.  
 Seconded by Mr. Badowski.  
Roll Call: Badowski, Miller, Murray, Perras, Tarbet, and Durand. 6-0 in favor. 
 
4. 24 Congress Street: Small Project Review – Facade painting, installation of tile trim, and new entry 
doors for Mexizol.  
 
Eddie Diaz was present to discuss the proposal: 
• A rendering of the proposal was shared.  
• The applicant wishes to change the color of the façade to a rich green and cream color with tile 
underneath. The brick would remain as is. There are no infrastructure changes proposed.  
• There are no changes proposed to the side of the building.  
• Mr. Durand noted support for the green color.  
• The windows on the parking lot side of the building would remain as is.  
• The two main doors at the front of the building are not operational and are proposed to be 
replaced.  
• The proposed doors are solid wood with a glass window.  
• The doors will remain the color shown in the photo.  
• Mr. Perras requested that if the applicant needs to come before the DRB again to show the 
entire façade as proposed. 
• No change to lighting is proposed.  
• Russell Tanzer highlighted the front entry doors that will be replaced.  
• There is no proposed plan to do anything on the river side of the building. 
 
There were no comments or questions from members of the public.  
 
 VOTE: Mr. Perras made a motion to approve the proposed changes.  
 Seconded by Ms. Miller.   
Roll Call: Badowski, Miller, Murray, Perras, and Durand. 5-0 in favor. 
*Note: Sarah Tarbet was not present for this vote due to internet/technical issues. 
 
Projects Outside of the Urban Renewal Area
DRB 
October 28, 2026 
Page 3 of 8 
 
 
1. 56 Margin Street, 54 Margin Street, 7 High Street, 20 Endicott Street, and 24 Endicott Street: Smart 
Growth Overlay District - Design review of the proposed project at Lifebridge Main Campus. The 
applicant proposes the demolition of the buildings at 24 Endicott Street and 56 Margin Street, the 
adaptive reuse of 54 Margin Street, and the preservation of the facade of 20 Endicott Street to 
accommodate for a 22,806 square foot building comprised of 53 affordable homes, a shelter with 70 
beds, and supportive programming space along with other site improvements. Thirteen parking 
spaces are proposed on site.  
 
Pat Connolly, Julie Reimenschneider, and Stefano Basso with SV Design were present to discuss the 
project:  
• Mr. Connolly reported that since the last meeting, Harborlight provided written responses to the 
last outstanding design criteria.  
• Ms. Reimenschneider shared the landscape plan.  
• They are proposing a permeable brick between the curb and the sidewalk. The sidewalk would 
be concrete. Nine new street trees are proposed. 
• The front of the building would have two brick patio spaces available to residents of the 
building. Benches are proposed for this space.  
• Between the patois and the public streetscape, a low wall with a metal, black steel fence is 
proposed with evergreen landscape plants to provide privacy and separation from the street.  
• There will be long planters that will include ornamental grasses, shrubs, and perennials that will 
coordinate with the columns on the building.  
• At the historic church entrance there will be plantings with a simple concrete ramp and set of 
stairs.  
• The street trees proposed are Morton Glossy Elm which was recommended by the Planning 
Board. The screening plants are Missouri Holly, Box Hedge Holly, and Oak Leaf Hydrangea. 
Junipers are proposed for the planters. Irrigation is not proposed.  
• Other proposed plants are daylilies, little bluestem, cat mint, and Shasta daisies.  
• The Memorial Plaza Garden would include a European orange beam tree and oak leaf 
hydrangea. 
• The landscape plans and plant list was shared and reviewed.  
• The back of the building is very narrow with a very high retaining wall. They are proposing a 
gravel surface. Maple leaf, viburnum, columnar red maples, and American hornbeam with 
groups of shrubs.  
• Ms. Miller inquired about the tree planting detail. Ms. Reimenschneider said they are proposing 
two feet of sand based structural soil, a geogrid and crushed stone to support the pavers. The 
brick surrounding the tree would not be filled in. An aluminum edge is proposed to support the 
pavers which can be pulled out as the tree grows.  
• Mr. Perras inquired about the railings. The construction drawing was shared. It would be black 
iron.  
• Mr. Perras inquired about the interstitial spaces in the back. Ms. Reimenschneider noted that 
there is not much access in the area and there is a very large retaining wall. The surface would 
be a low maintenance crushed stone with soil for the plants. There is a stone strip edge 
proposed along the side of the building. It is not an occupiable space. Ms. Reimenschneider said 
that anyone that has a window would be able to look out at the vegetation and it provides 
screening from the adjacent park.
DRB 
October 28, 2026 
Page 4 of 8 
 
 
There were no comments or questions from members of the public.  
 
• Ms. Owens noted that the project team provided materials including the sidewalk configuration, 
bicycle use, etc. that she shared with the board. 
• Mr. Basso said they’ve updated the colors to match the rest of the renderings.  
• Ms. Miller noted that she was happy that all the street trees are being replaced.  
• Mr. Basso said they dropped off physical samples of the brick sample and paint chips for review.  
• Mr. Basso reviewed the updated materials sheet. He said there were minor adjustments on the 
color scheme, including the brick colors to more accurately represent the church and the 20 
Endicott building on the corner.  
• Renderings were shared and reviewed. 
• Mr. Perras noted that the color of the corner building seems to be clashing with the tone and 
recommended a color closer to the headers of the windows and sills.  
• Mr. Perras asked if the siding boards could be wrapped or if they must use corner boards; that 
there is a lot of trim. Mr. Basso said they tend to use the corner board. Mr. Perras said it seemed 
like the corner boards may be excessive.  
• Ms. Miller noted that the corner building has come a long way. She asked if the back side the 
building, where it faces the playground, could have the same color corner elements, and have 
the trim be the same color.  
• Mr. Perras reiterated that he would rather see the trim minimized as much as possible. He 
would rather see it look more continuous. Mr. Basso said he believes it will read more subtle in 
person. Mr. Perras agreed and said it is likely a product of the rendering.  
• Mr. Basso said they would like to wrap up the public approvals process and then they would 
jump into design development, engineering, structural, and interior design.  
• Mr. Connolly said they are hoping to have Planning Board approval in the next week, and then 
they wait until they are funded.  
• Mr. Perras said this is the final time the project will come before the DRB.  
• Mr. Perras requested that the applicant look at the renderings and see what matching corner 
pieces look like.  
• Ms. Miller asked if the project could come back when they are at the design development stage.  
• Mr. Durand said for this project, they are giving their recommendations to the Planning Board.  
• Ms. Owens noted that this is a 40R project so there are time limits.   
• Ms. Tarbet asked if the applicant could update the renderings with the options discussed, and 
that the DRB could state in their decision that these are issues that they would like the Planning 
Board to review and weigh in on. Mr. Durand agreed on that approach.  
• Mr. Perras noted that the design has advanced greatly, and that there were just a couple of 
details he would like the Planning Board to review. Mr. Basso said they could put the options 
together for the Planning Board.  
• Signage was included the applicant’s response.  
 
 VOTE: Mr. Perras made a motion to approve what was presented, including the ongoing 
conversations on the design standards on the sidewalk configuration and bicycle use, and the 
options on the renderings where the corner board are minimalized so it appears that the façade
DRB 
October 28, 2026 
Page 5 of 8 
 
material is wrapping around the corner to be revised and approved or discussed by the Planning 
Board.  
 Seconded by Ms. Tarbet.  
Roll Call: Badowski, Miller, Murray, Perras, Tarbet, and Durand. 6-0 in favor. 
 
2.  16 Bridge Street: Bridge Street Neck Overlay District – Design review of a proposed two-family 
residential building.  
 
Adimir Toska was present to discuss the proposal:  
• Mr. Toska shared the plot plan. There is an existing building and a vacant lot where a two-family 
residence is proposed.  
• The project has been approved by the ZBA. 
• The drawings were shared. Each unit is proposed to be 1082 SF. There is no basement. There is a 
four-car parking garage.  
• The elevations and 3D versions were shared.  
• Mr. Toska is proposing vinyl windows, vinyl siding, asphalt shingles and roofing.  
• No color renderings were shared.  
• Ms. Owens noted that this project is located within Bridge Street Neck which falls under the DRB 
purview. The DRB’s review happens currently with the Planning Board. 
• Ms. Tarbet noted that she didn’t think the proposal meets many of the design guidelines. She 
said the intent of the overlay is to activate Bridge Street. She is most concerned about the side 
facing Bridge Street. 
• Ms. Tarbet noted that one of the main components is to minimize the appearance of parking, 
and the building has been designed around the garage. She does not believe the roof lines and 
front windows comply.  
• Mr. Toska said their intent was to mimic the building at 14 Bridge Street. 
• Ms. Tarbet said she could overlook the parking if the façade design was more contextual.  
• Ms. Miller noted that the DRB is concerned with windows, entries, and the face of the building.  
• Ms. Owens said she would reshare the design guidelines, compliance table, and standards with 
the applicant.  
• Ms. Tarbet noted that the materials proposed are not compliant, as vinyl and other synthetic 
materials is to be avoided.  
• Mr. Perras said the intention of the overlay district is to continue to improve conditions, not just 
mimic what is there.  
• The height matches the guidelines.  
• Mr. Toska said they are planning to bring a landscape architect on board.  
• Ms. Tarbet noted that the ordinance suggests that the Planning Board could waive the number 
of required parking spaces if that change would help with the design.  
• Mr. Toska said they have a civil engineer who is working on trash collection and stormwater 
detail.  
• Ms. Miller said it would be worth considering the cars coming off Hubon Street, and that 
changing the first floor so that the stars are running up would go a long way. 
• Ms. Miller said they will want to hear about landscape design.  
 
There were no comments or questions from members of the public.
DRB 
October 28, 2026 
Page 6 of 8 
 
 
 VOTE: Ms. Martin made a motion to continue.  
 Seconded by Ms. Tarbet.  
Roll Call: Badowski, Miller, Murray, Perras, Tarbet, and Durand. 6-0 in favor. 
 
3.   370 376 Highland Avenue, 378 380 Highland Avenue, and 382 Highland Avenue: Entrance Corridor  
      Overlay District – Design review of proposed car wash facility.  
 
Bob Griffin, Andrea Morton, and Frank Dougherty were present to review the proposal: 
• A map and aerial of the area was shared.  
• The proposal is to remove all the existing structures and to consolidate the three entrances into 
one entrance off Highland Avenue and one entrance on Savon Avenue.  
• A traffic loop is proposed with cars coming in off Highland with three pay stations.  
• This will be a staffed operation.  
• Washville washes cars through a tunnel, there are no self service bays. It will not be a 24-hr 
operation.  
• The 4300 SF site would include the building, vacuum equipment to reduce noise. There are 
approximately 20 vacuum stations proposed.  
• The landscape plan, created by Ulrich Design, was shared. It includes many planting beds and 
trees. Roughly twenty trees are proposed and include maples, dogwoods, and white pines. 
There will be grasses, perennials, and shrubs planted as well. The plant schedule was shared.  
• Ms. Morton shared and reviewed the various elevations of the building.  
• Gables, spandrel glass windows are proposed to be in keeping with the neighborhood.  
• The building includes an office, and roll-up doors. An elevated area will hold condensers. Any 
other RTUs are within the attic space.  
• Ms. Morton noted that some of the detailing harkens to a more residential style of New England 
design. They are endeavoring to keep many of the plantings in place and add additional 
plantings.  
• Ms. Morton said panel siding, intended to look like clapboard, is proposed. A standing seam, 
blue mental roof is proposed. There are a few pops of color that speak to the Washville brand.  
• Mr. Perras said he likes the darker blue better.  
• Ms. Morton said the color is custom and is a royal blue. She said they could provide a sample.  
• Mr. Perras and Ms. Murray agreed that there is appeal in the proposal of having different colors 
for the doors and roof.  
• Mr. Perras suggested keeping the roof darker. Ms. Morton said she would discuss it with the 
client.  
• All the outside equipment will be the blue color.  
• Ms. Murray noted that the roof on the Tyngsborough facility appeared very blue. Mr. Dougherty 
said he was happy to receive the feedback.  
• The current sign application proposes using the existing sign, but is still under consideration. 
• Ms. Miller noted concern about the stone veneer layer, and that perhaps having a bigger stone 
base may help it look more authentic.  
• Ms. Miller said she was pleased the edge was remaining. She asked that the slope be planted.
DRB

• In response to Ms. Miller’s question about both access points being on Highland Ave., Mr. Griffin 
said they are working on a traffic study to better understand the issues. Ms. Miller said it would 
be an improvement to the neighborhood if traffic could come in and off Highland Ave.  
• Ms. Miller said the second sign could be invasive to the neighborhood. Mr. Dougherty said it is 
more of a wayfinding sign. Ms. Miller said it will be helpful to revisit once they see what the site 
is going to look like.  
 
There were no comments or questions from members of the public.  
 
VOTE: Ms. Martin made a motion to continue with the topics that were discussed.  
 Seconded by Mr. Badowski  
Roll Call: Badowski, Miller, Murray, Perras, Tarbet, and Durand. 6-0 in favor. 
 
 
New/Old Business 
 
1. Approval of Minutes:  
a. September 9, 2026 
VOTE: Mr. Perras made a motion to approve the September 9th meeting minutes.   
Seconded by Ms. Miller.   
Roll Call: Badowski, Miller, Murray, Perras, Tarbet, and Durand. 6-0 in favor. 
 
b. September 23, 2026 
VOTE: Mr. Perras made a motion to approve the September 23rd meeting minutes.   
Seconded by Ms. Miller.   
Roll Call: Badowski, Miller, Murray, Perras, Tarbet, and Durand. 6-0 in favor. 
 
 
2. Staff Updates 
 
 
 Upcoming Meetings 
 
1. SRA: November 4 – Note that this date is one week earlier than normal due to Veterans Day.  
2. DRB: November 18 – Note that this date is one week earlier than normal due to Thanksgiving.  
  
 
Adjournment 
 
VOTE: Mr. Perras made a motion to adjourn.  Second: Ms. Miller. All in favor.  
 
The meeting adjourned at 7:33PM.
